summary: All three r1 criticals and all five warnings are genuinely folded into the r2 body and are CORRECT against the code, not just the changelog. CRIT-1: saxpy (verified examples/saxpy.axc) writes y[i] UNCONDITIONALLY with an alpha:f32 push-constant, so alpha is the sole annihilation vector; r2 pins alpha=2.0, FORBIDS silent zero-fill for float-scalar kernels (push_constants_required ERROR, AT-2850b), and AT-2855 adds an explicit, clearly-LABELED alpha=0 negative control (not counted among the ACCEPT fixtures AT-2851/2852/2858/2859). The non-vacuity n_diff>0 guard reads the report's own comparison field and is complemented by the alpha=0 control that PASSes — not circular. CRIT-2: server-owned BitExact default + loud tolerance_overridden stamp; bit-exact is VERIFIED usable for both accept pairs (cached-vs-cached_sr is bit-identical because strength-reduction touches only integer index math; matmul-vs-pad plain-f32 is n_diff=0/589824 per the M3.10a merged record) and the tolerance-needing q4km pad pair is correctly NOT used as an accept fixture. CRIT-3: the [-1,1] formula is exact and implementable, and the 'existing half-float path' is REAL — half="2" is a direct dependency of axc-driver (Cargo.toml:224), so half::f16::from_f32(v).to_bits() is reachable from rewrite_verify.rs; raw-byte fill correctly retained for integer/packed only. WARN-1: derive_workgroups confirmed 1-D/4-byte-only, so mandatory explicit workgroups for coopmat/shared is the right hard-ERROR and the elementwise --size path stays coherent. WARN-2: the determinism self-check dispatches the ORIGINAL twice against the SINGLE shared input set (bit-exact self-compare) → NONDETERMINISTIC_ORACLE, a clean 'no verdict', not a false FAIL. WARN-3: the closed verdict/reason taxonomy maps every reachable error path incl. preflight_fail_rewritten, original-side SKIPPED/infra, and infra_error. WARN-4/5: tail-K AT-2858 (with an explicit deferral clause) and the Lavapipe saxpy_reassoc ACCEPT path (commutation is IEEE-754 bit-identical for finite inputs) both land. AT range holds at <=2860. The residual items below are honest-scope observations already documented as limitations/non-goals — none blocks. APPROVE.

warnings: RESIDUAL (non-blocking) — CRIT-3 claim 'NaN-payload comparison thereby avoided for v1' is slightly OVERSTATED. The float ELEMENT buffers are now NaN-free, but the raw-byte fill for the packed Q4_K buffer still embeds f16 header scales (d, dmin) that CAN be random NaN/Inf, which propagate to NaN in the dequant→coopmat output. This does NOT bite the only q4km accept pair (cached vs cached_sr are float-bit-identical → identical NaN payload → bit-exact PASS), so v1 is safe. But the sentence should be scoped to 'float element buffers'; a FUTURE q4km REJECT fixture that is numerically divergent could face two-different-NaN-payload ambiguity. Worth a one-line caveat in §3.2 or §10.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking) — AT-2858 tail-K is a DISPATCH smoke test, not a CATCH test. Because cached vs cached_sr are bit-identical for ALL K by construction (strength reduction is integer-index-only), any tail-superblock mishandling would be present in BOTH kernels (shared-oracle-blindness) and still PASS. So the AT proves the harness RUNS at K%256≠0, not that it would CATCH a tail-mishandling rewrite. The §8 framing ('exercising the partial-final-superblock decode path where Q4_K_M bugs historically live') slightly oversells what a bit-identical pair can verify. Acceptable for v1 given the deferral clause and the documented shared-oracle limitation; consider softening the AT-2858 prose to 'exercises tail-K dispatch' rather than implying bug-detection.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking) — the tolerance_overridden contract is EMITTED (in-scope, tested via AT-2849/2860) but its ENFORCEMENT depends on the outer supervisor gating on the flag, which this milestone does not add. §4.2 states the supervisor 'CAN and does audit' — that is an expectation, not code shipped here. This is honestly scoped (non-goal #10, 'governed not eliminated') and the loud-stamp satisfies my r1 ask, so it does not block; just note that the guarantee delivered is 'non-silent', not 'prevented'.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking) — the determinism self-check compares original-vs-original BIT-EXACT regardless of the requested tolerance. A kernel that is deterministic-within-tolerance but bitwise-nondeterministic run-to-run (e.g. an unordered-but-bounded reduction) would be flagged NONDETERMINISTIC_ORACLE even under rel:1e-3, yielding 'no verdict' for a kernel the caller might consider verifiable. This is the conservative/correct outcome (it renders no-verdict, never a false FAIL) and is covered by non-goal #8, so it stands — just flagging the boundary of the 'verifiable-kernel' set.

The coopmat accept fixtures (AT-2851/2852/2858) remain NVIDIA-tier and typed-skip on Lavapipe (AT-2857), which is correct.
questions_for_architect: NON-BLOCKING nit: the header says 'AT range: AT-2841 … AT-2860' (20 ATs) but the body enumerates 21 entries because of the sub-lettered AT-2850b. That is a legal sub-ID and does not exceed 2860 or collide, but consider either renumbering AT-2850b or noting the sub-ID convention in the header for bookkeeping cleanliness.

NON-BLOCKING nit: examples/saxpy_reassoc.axc is named 'reassoc' but the described transform (y[i]=y[i]+alpha*x[i]) is a COMMUTATION of the final add, not a re-association (which would NOT be IEEE bit-safe). The transform as written IS bit-identical; only the fixture name is mildly misleading — consider 'saxpy_commute' to prevent a future reader assuming true reassociation is being claimed bit-exact.
